title: Chart data
description: What a chart draws: named tables of typed columns and named matrices (REQ-DATA-010). In JSON every column carries its values; through the binary API (typed arrays, Arrow IPC) the same descriptor travels without `values` and the values arrive as buffers (REQ-DATA-050). Two shorthands, an object of arrays and an array of row objects, are normalised by the shell to the full form before anything crosses into wasm (REQ-DATA-120). The schema does not check that every column of a table has the same length, that `sorted` names a column, or that edge indexes are within `nodes`; the shell checks these and warns.

name.description: A table, matrix or column name: a letter or underscore, then up to 63 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`.

data.description: The full form of the data contract.

tables.description: Tables by name. A chart that draws one table takes the first; a graph takes `nodes` and `edges` (REQ-DATA-160).

matrices.description: Matrices by name, for heatmaps and adjacency matrices.

table.description: A table of columns, all of one length.

length.description: Rows. Required when no column carries values; otherwise every column's values have this length.

sorted.description: A column the rows are in non-decreasing order of. The chart verifies it on load and sorts a copy if it is wrong (REQ-DATA-040).

frame.description: The coordinate frame of the table's angle or position columns (roles ra/dec, lon/lat, az/alt, x/y/z). Angles are degrees; distances are au unless a column's `unit` says otherwise.

epoch.description: The equinox or epoch of a celestial frame, as `J2000` or an RFC 3339 date-time.

columns.description: The table's columns, 1 to 256, in order.

column.description: One typed column. Numbers, timestamps and durations are held as f64 in the chart (REQ-DATA-020); missing values become NaN, or u32::MAX for categories (REQ-DATA-030).

name.description: The column's name, unique in its table.

type.description: f64, f32, i64 and u32 are numbers; timestamp is an instant since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z in `time_unit`; duration is a span in `time_unit`; category is an index into `categories`; string is a free label per row.

role.description: What the column is to a chart. A chart finds each channel by the option `encode`, then by `role`, then by a column of that name (REQ-DATA-080).

unit.description: The unit of the values for display and formatting (`USD`, `°C`, `B/s`, `%`). Not a conversion.

scale.description: Displayed value = stored value × scale + offset (prices in integer cents: scale 0.01). Applies to ticks, readouts and the table, never to stored values (REQ-DATA-100).

offset.description: Added to the stored value times `scale` for display; default 0.

time_unit.description: For timestamp and duration columns; default ms. A `us` or `ns` timestamp column is held as offsets from an i64 origin (REQ-DATA-020).

zone.description: For timestamp columns: the IANA zone (`America/New_York`) or `UTC` in which ticks and labels are drawn. Values are UTC instants whatever the zone; default UTC (REQ-DATA-090).

categories.description: For category columns: the labels the values index, in legend order.

values.description: The column's values in JSON. null is missing: NaN for a number or time, no category, an empty label. A timestamp may be a number in `time_unit` or an RFC 3339 string. Absent when the values arrive as a buffer.

matrix.description: A row-major matrix of rows × cols numbers (REQ-DATA-160).

values.description: rows × cols values, row by row; null is missing. Absent when the values arrive as a buffer.

row_labels.description: A label for each row, top to bottom.

col_labels.description: A label for each column, left to right.

unit.description: The unit of the values for display, as a column's `unit`.

symmetric.description: An adjacency matrix of an undirected graph: only the upper triangle is read.

columnsShorthand.description: `{"t": [...], "close": [...]}`: one table of columns by name. Types are inferred: numbers f64, RFC 3339 strings timestamps (ms, UTC), other strings categories, booleans bool.

rowsShorthand.description: `[{"t": ..., "close": ...}, ...]`: one table of rows, turned into columns by the shell with the same inference as the columns shorthand.
